title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
The intersection of AI, big business, and the economy dominated the conversation this week.

AI spending is starting to make investors nervous. Both Alphabet and Tesla saw their stocks take a hit this week as heavy investments in AI drained free cash flow. Wall Street is now watching closely to see if Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon will face similar pressure. Meanwhile, the Trump administration appears to be shifting its stance on AI regulation. Following recent hacking incidents at OpenAI, officials are reportedly considering new controls on the technology, marking a departure from their previous hands-off approach.

In the consumer space, Meta is integrating its AI chatbot directly into Threads direct messages. For Apple, the focus is on hardware access. The company launched a new device leasing program with Klarna, aimed at helping users upgrade their gear despite ongoing industry-wide memory chip shortages.

In the UK, retail is seeing a significant shift. Chinese robotics firms are moving in to fill gaps left by labor shortages and stagnant productivity, deploying robot fleets to handle retail operations.

On the economic front, the Federal Reserve held US interest rates steady between 3.5% and 3.75%. Fed leadership emphasized that there is no quick fix for high prices. The bond market remains skeptical, however. Investor Jeffrey Gundlach noted that movements across the Treasury curve suggest the market doubts the Fed will follow through on its inflation targets.

Finally, Johnson & Johnson has proposed a settlement of up to $5.5 billion to resolve long-standing legal battles over claims that its talc products are linked to cancer.
